Article Title: 'Wrong message to society': Rijiju attacks Rahul Gandhi over Gyanesh Kumar resignation demand
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi had alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged”.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday attacked leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of the Election Commission and demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, saying such remarks would send a “wrong message to society”.Speaking to reporters, Rijiju said, “It is not appropriate to amplify Rahul Gandhi's remarks in the public sphere, as it would send the wrong message to society.”His remarks came days after Rahul Gandhi stepped up his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul had alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” and demanded the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.Addressing a press conference at the Congress headquarters on Thursday, the Congress leader accused the Election Commission of failing to protect voters’ rights and alleged that the electoral process had been compromised.“Mr Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately. We are not going to let democracy be destroyed in India and sit silent, and the people responsible for this are going to be punished,” the Rae Bareli MP said.Rahul also referred to reports that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections on several occasions over decisions related to electoral-roll management and the SIR exercise.“The two Election Commissioners have done a wise thing, and I appreciate it,” he said. Rahul further alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were “at the top of this conspiracy” and would be investigated. He also said Kumar should “turn approver”.“I can say with certainty that Indian elections -- 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha polls -- were all rigged,” Rahul said. He also linked his allegations over electoral rolls to the functioning of Parliament and other institutions.“From vote chori (vote theft), comes kanoon chori (law theft) and from that comes sanstha chori (institutional theft),” he said.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections reflected a disagreement over its final decisions.The poll panel said on Saturday that key decisions related to the SIR, including orders and schedules, were taken with the “unanimous approval” of all three commissioners.It also clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary, which had drawn scrutiny, concerned the functioning of an officer on deputation to the ECI and was not related to any policy matter, ANI reported.The clarification came after an Indian Express report said that Sandhu and Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on issues including voter registration, deletion and restoration of names, changes to Form 6 and access to electoral-roll databases.The ECI said the SIR order issued on June 24, 2025, covering all states and Union territories, was approved unanimously. It also said the schedules for subsequent phases were issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission.Earlier in the day, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath also criticised the Congress and its allies over their attacks on the Election Commission and the SIR.“Congress and its allies should apologise to the constitutional institutions of the country and to the people for their actions,” Adityanath said.He said the SIR was not being conducted for the first time and pointed to earlier exercises carried out in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965-66 and 2003.“Despite all this, the kind of uproar that the Congress, Samajwadi Party, RJD and other parties have created over the SIR this time is extremely unfortunate,” he added.Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also criticised the opposition over its demand for Kumar’s resignation. He alleged that Congress and its allies question the credibility of the Election Commission and EVMs after losing elections.“We are seeing what is happening. When the Congress wins in Telangana, Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh and Kerala, the Opposition does not comment on the Election Commission,” Shinde added.The political row comes amid continuing scrutiny of the Election Commission’s handling of the SIR. Opposition parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT), have demanded Kumar’s resignation.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi had alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” and demanded the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Rijiju: “It is not appropriate to amplify Rahul Gandhi's remarks in the public sphere, as it would send the wrong message to society”

Article Title: 'Just another calm': Rahul Gandhi shares 'rough sea' message

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi during a press conference, at AICC headquarters, in New Delhi.

It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm,” Gandhi posted on X.Gandhi did not directly mention the SIR controversy or the Election Commission in the post. Article Title: Kharge, Sonia and Rahul pay homage to late PM Manmohan Singh
Article Text:
Congress leaders paid homage to former PM Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: Remembering him as a statesman and a visionary, Congress netas Mallikarjun Kharge Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi Saturday led the party in paying homage to late Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on his birth anniversary.Congress held a ceremony at the party office where the Gandhis, senior functionaries and office-bearers paid floral tributes to Singh. A prayer meeting was also organised by Singh's family at their residence, which was attended by Rahul.On the occasion, All India Professionals Congress announced the second batch of "Dr Manmohan Singh fellows program", under which professionals join the party to work on issues ranging from policy to politics. Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty and AIPC chairman Madhu Yaskhi Goud said the first batch had 50 fellows, while the second batch has been scaled up to 100.
Article Summary: Congress held a ceremony at the party office where the Gandhis, senior functionaries and office-bearers paid floral tributes to Singh. A prayer meeting was also organised by Singh's family at their residence, attended by Rahul. All India Professionals Congress announced the second batch of "Dr Manmohan Singh fellows program"

Article Title: J&K BJP bigwig meets Shah day after Omar moves statehood resolution with autonomy reference
Article Text:
Sunil Sharma meets HM Amit Shah in New Delhi

SRINAGAR: A day after CM Omar Abdullah moved an assembly resolution for restoration of J&K’s statehood with a reference to a similar document of the year 2000 on autonomy, BJP leader of opposition Sunil Sharma met Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday for “advice” even as PDP upped the ante and sought an amendment to condemn Article 370’s abrogation.Vowing to block the resolution, Sharma said Shah “reaffirmed the Union govt’s unwavering commitment to peace, development and prosperity of Jammu and Kashmir”.Sharma made it clear that BJP was prepared to debate the statehood restoration document brought by the Omar-led National Conference (NC) govt but would not accept attempts to “smuggle in” issues of Article 370 and the 2000 autonomy resolution.“When the (Omar-led) govt has lost its strength on governance, an attempt is being made to recover that by invoking references designed to stir emotion among the people of Kashmir. At no cost will the so-called autonomy resolution or Article 370 be allowed to become part of this debate,” Sharma said.PDP would have none of it. It called Friday’s resolution “weak” and demanded that the document begin with a denunciation of Article 370’s revocation by the Centre on Aug 5, 2019. PDP legislator Muntazir Mehdi disclosed that he had moved an amendment calling on the House to “express its deep anguish over the unilateral measures” of 2019 and urging the Centre to ensure “immediate restoration of J&K’s full statehood along with its constitutional safeguards”.Omar had moved the resolution amid a BJP backlash to the autonomy reference, with its members ripping up copies amid anti-national chants directed at NC. MLAs of NC ally Congress supported the resolution and confronted rivals. CPM, Peoples Conference and PDP also backed the resolution. The autonomy resolution was passed by the assembly in June 2000 when J&K was a state.Explaining the reference to previous resolutions, Omar said the aim was to convey that the House continued to stand by all past decisions. He rejected BJP’s charges, asked “how demanding statehood can be anti-national” and pointed out that statehood was a promise made by the Centre and reaffirmed by PM Narendra Modi at an event where BJP’s Sharma was present.Omar has been under pressure for months now, accused by rivals of dropping demands to restore Article 370 and demanding statehood only. On Saturday, NC spokesperson Tanvir called the resolution a powerful reminder that the party had “not forgotten” its agenda. BJP MLA Devyani Rana accused NC of raking up 25-year-old autonomy demands on the pretext of statehood.
Article Summary: BJP leader of opposition Sunil Sharma met Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday for ‘advice’ Sharma said Shah “reaffirmed the Union govt’s unwavering commitment to peace, development and prosperity of Jammu and Kashmir”

Article Title: PM Modi, HM Shah put CEC in charge of match-fixing elections: Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi calls CEC Gyanesh Kumar a ‘BJP headhunter’

NEW DELHI: With a top former bureaucrat of Kerala reportedly saying that chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had approached him to contest election on BJP ticket, leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi Saturday mocked that the poll panel chief was a headhunter for BJP and then put in charge of fixing polls."First, Gyanesh Kumar - then a serving IAS officer - was used to recruit for BJP. Then PM Modi and Shah made him the umpire and put him in charge of match-fixing India's elections," the Congress functionary posted on X, referring to the media reports.Meanwhile, Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh dismissed the Election Commission 's response to the recent media revelations. "Election Commission is in damage control mode after it has already caused massive damage to our democracy. It has just issued a wishy-washy press note that raises further questions on its intent, integrity, impartiality and credibility."
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi calls CEC Gyanesh Kumar a ‘BJP headhunter’ CEC reportedly approached him to contest election on BJP ticket. Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh dismissed the Election Commission's response to the recent media revelations.

Article Title: SIR row: Congress' Khera questions EC over Form 6, says Bengal & Bihar polls ‘illegal’
Article Text:
EC issues clarification on SIR

Questions Form 6 changes

What is the Form 6 row?

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Sunday questioned the Election Commission 's response to concerns over Form 6, claiming that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was based on a change to the form that could not have been made without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.Speaking to news agency PTI, Khera said the rules could not be changed without being amended in Parliament and questioned whether the Election Commission had addressed the objections raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi."The 1960 Rules cannot be changed without being amended in Parliament. The biggest point of difference between Sandhu ji and Joshi with Gyanesh Kumar was this, and did we receive the answer to it today?" Khera said.Khera alleged that the SIR exercise was based on an "illegally changed" Form 6 and questioned the validity of elections conducted in Bengal and Bihar on the basis of the exercise."The entire SIR is based on a Form 6 that was changed illegally. The SIR that arose from that illegal form has also become illegal. The elections held in Bengal and Bihar based on that illegal SIR have also become illegal. Did we get an answer on this?" he said.The controversy centres on the requirement for new voters to provide details linking themselves or their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls from the previous SIR.According to Indian Express reports, Election Commissioners Joshi and Sandhu had objected to incorporating the requirement into Form 6, arguing that the statutory form could not be altered without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.The Election Commission, however, has maintained that there was "no change" to Form 6 and that the SIR-related requirement was an additional declaration prescribed under its SIR orders. The poll panel has also said the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera questions the Election Commission's response to concerns over Form 6. He claims that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was based on a change to the form that could not have been made without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The controversy centres on the requirement for new voters to provide details linking themselves or their parents or grandparents to previous SIR.

Article Title: INDIA bloc to meet on Sept 30, CEC's ouster on top of agenda
Article Text:
Opposition INDIA bloc parties will meet on September 30 to discuss alleged poll-roll manipulation under the SIR process and a possible joint campaign seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.

NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc will meet on Sept 30 to discuss the alleged manipulation of poll rolls under SIR and a possible joint struggle to press for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The meeting has been scheduled against the backdrop of nationwide outrage triggered by revelations that ECs SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had questioned many of the decisions regarding SIR.The opposition, led by Rahul Gandhi, has said the revelations tie in with their allegations of 'vote chori' in favour of BJP over the last two years. It has demanded the scrapping of the SIR process.TMC MP Derek O'Brien said the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation is "non-negotiable", while other issues will also be discussed at the meeting. "We will work unitedly and purposefully."The meeting is expected to be attended by the leading lights of the anti-BJP front, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Uddhav Thackeray and MA Baby.The meeting has been scheduled after CPM's MA Baby wrote to parties (including AAP, DMK and CJP) seeking an immediate meeting.Trinamool's Mamata Banerjee also reached out to INDIA bloc members.She called the CEC "Vanish Kumar", demanded his ouster and said the Bengal mandate was stolen.The joint brainstorming will follow a Congress Working Committee meet on Sept 29.The parties are also planning to submit a fresh "removal notice" against Kumar in both Houses of Parliament.CPI-ML's Dipankar Bhattacharya said that there is a strong belief within INDIA bloc that some parties (Aam Aadmi Party and DMK) which are not part of the alliance umbrella should also be roped in to boost the campaign. It also released a fact-finding report regarding SIR in constituencies that the party lost narrowly in recent Bihar assembly polls and claimed it found 17-25% of voters had been wrongly deleted.The meeting assumes special significance as Cockroach Janata Party and other youth outfits have already announced a stir over the issue.CJP has reiterated that it will launch a nationwide agitation from Mumbai on Oct 2 after its ultimatum seeking the resignation of Kumar ended Saturday. Azad Maidan is most likely to be the venue of its protest.
Article Summary: Opposition INDIA bloc parties will meet on September 30 to discuss alleged poll- roll manipulation under the SIR process. Meeting is expected to be attended by the leading lights of the anti-BJP front, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee and Akhilesh Yadav.

Article Title: 'Truth has come to light': BJP after EC clarifies 'no rift' over electoral roll revision
Article Text:
BJP MP Sambit Patra criticises opposition for alleging BJP-ECI 'collusion' (File photo)

NEW DELHI: The ruling BJP on Saturday said that the Election Commission of India 's (ECI) statement on the SIR row has "clearly established" that the decision to conduct a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was taken with the full consensus of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two election commissioners."In the recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions including SIR across the country. The order for the SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all the States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The same has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 27.5.2026. The schedule for SIR for 12 States and UTs was issued on 27.10.2025 and those for 19 States/UTs was issued on 14.05.2026 with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The final figure of number of electors will be known only after final publication in the remaining 12 states of Phase-III," the poll panel's statement read.The ECI response and Patra's subsequent remarks came amid a political row over the SIR exercise following an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the roll revision process.“ECI's letter has now clearly established that the SIR was conducted with the signatures and full consensus of all three commissioners... The Supreme Court ruled in favour of the SIR... The public statement issued today by the Election Commission contains a photograph on its final page showing all three commissioners sitting together. Regarding the attacks that were being made on the Election Commission, the truth has clearly come to light today,” BJP MP Sambit Patra told news agency ANI.Patra also criticised the Congress-led opposition for alleging “collusion” between the BJP and the ECI.“Various opposition parties and the Congress Party in particular launched an aggressive attack on the Election Commission of India and the BJP. They alleged collusion between the Election Commission and the BJP, claiming that India's democracy was being compromised. The manner in which the Congress Party has attempted to launch an attack clearly demonstrates a lack of maturity within the party, as well as a nefarious design to undermine the Constitution,” the Puri MP added.Patra further accused the Congress of repeatedly targeting constitutional and other institutions, alleging that the party had questioned the credibility of various bodies since 2014.“Looking at the history of the Congress party since 2014, there is not a single institution that the party has not attacked. No other political party in India has attacked the Indian Army. But the Congress party and some of its allied ‘satellite’ parties have indeed attacked the Indian Army.”Opposition parties, including the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), Shiv Sena (UBT) and Left parties, have intensified their criticism of the ECI, raising concerns over electoral transparency and demanding accountability.Congress units in several states, including Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, Assam, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Manipur, also staged protests over the issue.The Election Commission, meanwhile, has maintained that internal technical notes and written queries are part of the normal functioning of a multi-member body. It has also asserted that all final decisions related to the SIR process were taken unanimously and had the approval of all three commissioners.The Congress has indicated that opposition parties may move a fresh impeachment motion against CEC Kumar in Parliament. The issue is expected to come up at the Congress Working Committee meeting scheduled for September 29 in New Delhi.
Article Summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra criticises opposition for alleging BJP-ECI 'collusion' Patra also accuses Congress of repeatedly targeting constitutional and other institutions. Congress has indicated that opposition parties may move a fresh impeachment motion against CEC Kumar in Parliament.

Article Title: 'EC held SIR to help BJP capture Bengal': Mamata guns for CEC, says protest will go on till he resigns
Article Text:
Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Saturday alleged that the Election Commission conducted the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to "help the BJP capture Bengal" by deleting names of valid voters. She further demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“The truth is now out about how BJP used EC,” Banerjee said, in an apparent reference to a recent report on differences within the poll panel over the SIR exercise.Speaking at a rally in Serampore, Banerjee said protests would continue until Kumar stepped down.“Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar must resign, otherwise protests will continue,” news agency PTI quoted her as saying.Moreover, Mamata confirmed that INDIA bloc meeting was likely to be held in Delhi's Constitution Club on September 30.The proposed meeting comes amid closer coordination among the parties following reports of differences within the poll panel over aspects of the SIR exercise. The parties have been consulting each other on the issue and are working on a possible joint response.Earlier, Banerjee had alleged that leaders and workers of her faction of the Trinamool Congress had been kept under house arrest to prevent them from attending the rally, while BJP workers had “taken over the route” to the venue.“We have been kept under house arrest. I am not allowed to go to the venue of the rally. But I will go and address the rally. Stop me if you can,” she said before leaving for the venue.Banerjee took an alternative route through Dankuni and Delhi Road to reach Serampore instead of Uttarpara. A police vehicle accompanied her convoy.“BJP goons have taken over the route to the rally venue. There are no police personnel,” she alleged, referring to an alleged attack on TMC leaders travelling to the rally.Stones and eggs were allegedly thrown at TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh's car in Uttarpara as he travelled to the rally. A group carrying black flags reportedly surrounded his vehicle and shouted the “go black” slogan. Central forces were subsequently deployed in the area.Banerjee accused the police and administration of failing to act against those responsible.“Such atrocities are seen in African countries. Such atrocities are not even happening in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, which are also BJP-ruled. Then why has the ruling BJP unleashed so much terror on the streets (here)?” she said.The West Bengal BJP rejected Banerjee's allegations as baseless.“When the people of the state have already rejected Mamata Banerjee and TMC in assembly elections, why would BJP attack them? No BJP workers was involved in the attack on Ghosh,” West Bengal BJP spokesperson Debjit Sarkar said.
Article Summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee alleged that the Election Commission conducted the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to "help the BJP capture Bengal" She further demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Mamata confirmed that INDIA bloc meeting was likely to be held in Delhi's Constitution Club on September 30.

Article Title: CJP to launch nationwide stir as CEC ‘deadline’ ends
Article Text:
Cockroach Janata Party intends to launch a nationwide protest from Mumbai on October 2

TOI





MUMBAI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has reiterated that it will launch a nationwide agitation from Mumbai on Oct 2 after its ultimatum seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar ended Saturday.CJP held a meeting in Delhi Saturday where it was finalised, a member said. Azad Maidan is most likely to be the venue of its protest.Opposition parties are sceptical about joining the agitation. MNS chief Raj Thackeray said his party with his alliance partner, Shiv Sena (UBT), will organise a protest in Mumbai from Oct 4, though UBT MLA Aaditya Thackeray supported the Oct 2 protest. Congress too has planned a separate protest across the country to highlight their ‘vote-chori’ allegation instead of joining the CJP protest.Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee will hold protests across the state on Monday, Sept 28, demanding that Gyanesh Kumar be dismissed from service and arrested. Congress functionaries are asked to protest in their respective districts on Monday.Meanwhile, responding to the CJP’s announcement, Aaditya said, “If Gyanesh doesn’t go, Mumbai will step out against Vote Chori from 2nd October, in huge numbers!!”“Thank you, Aaditya Thackeray, for extending your support to our call to save democracy.All Indians, irrespective of their political parties or ideologies, must come together against SIR,” said Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder and convener, in reply to Aaditya’s post on X.CJP had demanded Kumar’s resignation after election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had reportedly raised questions about Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls but were not taken into account; the two election commissioners had reportedly filed dissenting objections to institutional policies over a 10-month period.A CJP member said the Mumbai venue hasn’t been finalised because no police permission has been received, but it is most likely going to be Azad Maidan. Akshay Shinde, the national secretary (organisation), toldthey will continue trying for permission. Speaking on the protest, a CJP member said they had held off calling the stir sooner because of Ganeshotsav, especially in Pune and Mumbai. CJP members say the organisation has more than 500 official members just in Mumbai, giving them the necessary organisational strength to execute the planned agitations effectively.
Article Summary: CJP held a meeting in Delhi Saturday where it was finalised, a member said. Azad Maidan is most likely to be the venue of its protest. Opposition parties are sceptical about joining the agitation. MNS chief Raj Thackeray said his party with his alliance partner, Shiv Sena (UBT), will organise a protest in Mumbai from Oct 4.

Article Title: Social media influencer booked for assaulting ex-Pune cantonment medical officer, demanding Rs 5 lakh
Article Text:
The complainant suffered injuries during the attack.





PUNE: Kalepadal police have booked a social media influencer and a contestant at a prominent Marathi reality show, along with her accomplices, for allegedly barging into the house of a 65-year-old former chief medical officer (CMO) of Pune Cantonment Hospital, assaulting him with sharp weapons, and demanding Rs5 lakh for purportedly publicising an event at Bal Gandharva Rangmandir.The complainant suffered injuries during the attack. After recovering, he lodged an FIR against the influencer, a resident of Sinhagad Road, and her 10 accomplices at Kalepadal police station on Friday. According to the police, the complainant retired as the chief medical officer (CMO) of the Pune Cantonment Hospital in 2021 and is a member of a social foundation. The organisation conducted a function at Bal Gandharva Rangmandir from Sept 1 to 3. Neither the complainant nor the organisation had officially invited the reel star to the event, nor had anyone asked her to publicise it. However, claiming that she had publicised the event, she began demanding Rs5 lakh from the complainant through phone calls and messages starting in Aug.On Sept 17, the influencer and several associates went to the complainant’s house. Since he was not at home, they allegedly threatened his wife and son before leaving. On Sept 23, the suspects called the complainant to an eatery where they again demanded money. The next day, the influencer and her accomplices barged into his home and assaulted him, police said.
Article Summary: The complainant suffered injuries during the attack. After recovering, he lodged an FIR against the influencer and her 10 accomplices. The complainant retired as the chief medical officer (CMO) of the Pune Cantonment Hospital in 2021.

Article Title: Yet another judge recuses in IFS officer Chaturvedi’s case, tally at 17
Article Text:
The matter was being considered in light of a SC ruling delivered in May 2025.





DEHRADUN: A judicial member of Central Administrative Tribunal’s (CAT) Delhi bench has recused himself from hearing a petition filed by Uttarakhand-cadre IFS officer Sanjiv Chaturvedi, taking the number of judges who have withdrawn from cases involving the officer to 17 across Supreme Court , Uttarakhand high court, CAT and district judiciary.The latest recusal came from Justice Rajveer Singh Verma while hearing Chaturvedi’s challenge to a Nov 2021 Uttarakhand govt order concerning the channel for appraisal reports of IFS officers. The matter was being considered in light of a SC ruling delivered in May 2025.In its Sept 21 order, the CAT bench recorded, “After hearing the matter for some time, Rajveer Singh Verma, member (J), recuses himself from hearing this matter.” The order did not specify a reason for the recusal, as has also been the case with several earlier recusals in matters involving Chaturvedi.The 17 judges who have recused themselves over the years include two SC judges, four Uttarakhand HC judges, nine CAT judges, including a former CAT chairperson, and two district judiciary judges. Most of the 17 recusal orders did not record specific reasons for judges withdrawing from the cases.The most recent high court recusals came in Sept and Oct 2025, when Justice Alok Verma and Justice Ravindra Maithani withdrew from hearing a contempt petition filed by Chaturvedi against CAT members and tribunal registry. The petition alleged wilful disobedience of a stay order passed by high court.In Feb 2024, Justice Manoj Tiwari recused from a case concerning the summoning of documents from appointments committee of the cabinet relating to Chaturvedi’s central deputation. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal had recused in May 2023 from another matter concerning records linked to anti-corruption investigations conducted by Chaturvedi during his tenure as chief vigilance officer at AIIMS, Delhi.CAT has seen a series of recusals as well. In Feb 2025, a bench comprising Harvinder Oberai and B Anand withdrew from a case concerning the alleged downgrading of Chaturvedi’s appraisal report by then Union health minister JP Nadda . The bench also directed that Chaturvedi’s cases should not be listed before it in future.Earlier CAT recusals included then chairperson Justice L Narasimhan Reddy in 2019, Justice RN Singh in 2021, and a bench comprising Manish Garg and Chhabilendra Roul in 2023. Justice Rajeev Joshi recused from a matter involving Chaturvedi in Jan 2025 .The sequence dates back to Nov 2013, when then SC judge Justice Ranjan Gogoi recused from Chaturvedi’s petition seeking a CBI probe into alleged corruption and harassment during his Haryana tenure. Justice UU Lalit subsequently recused from the same matter in Aug 2016.
Article Summary: The latest recusal came from Justice Rajveer Singh Verma while hearing Chaturvedi’s challenge to a Uttarakhand govt order concerning the channel for appraisal reports of IFS officers. The matter was being considered in light of a SC ruling delivered in May 2025.

Article Title: DMK MP seeks action against Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, minister Aadhav Arjuna for ‘violating’ model code of conduct
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay

‘DMK accuse TVK govt attempt to save their family friend Veeramani’





CHENNAI: DMK Rajya Sabha member J Constandine Ravindran on Saturday petitioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and chief electoral officer Archana Patnaik, seeking action against Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and TVK leader Aadhav Arjuna for allegedly violating the model code of conduct and a Madras high court order restraining them from making remarks about the DMK and its leaders in connection with a POCSO case against granite baron R Veeramani.Ravindran accused Vijay of repeatedly referring to the sensitive case during his Madurantakam election campaign despite the court order. He said the CM's remarks showed that the TVK leadership was disregarding the court's directions and the rule of law. “We have submitted a petition to the chief electoral officer, demanding immediate action against them,” he said.The DMK MP alleged that the ruling party was distributing money to voters in Madurantakam and had submitted a complaint with video evidence. He further accused TVK leaders of using govt vehicles for election campaigns and involving schoolchildren in their campaign. He urged the Election Commission to intervene to ensure a free and fair bypoll.Responding to Vijay's allegations that the previous DMK govt had tried to cover up the POCSO case against Veeramani, Ravindran alleged that TVK ministers had maintained cordial relations with the accused, with one of them describing him as a “family friend.”He accused the state police, under the TVK govt, of repeatedly seeking adjournments in the case to protect Veeramani. The judge was unhappy with the repeated delays and ordered his arrest on Aug 27, he said and noted that it was not the other way around as claimed by the CM.“Vijay acted to save himself after his attempt to cover up the case was exposed. He is now diverting the issue by blaming the DMK. People are watching everything, and they are not fools,” Ravindran said.He said the police and the entire govt machinery were under the control of the TVK govt and demanded a thorough investigation and stringent action against everyone involved in the case.
Article Summary: DMK Rajya Sabha member J Constandine Ravindran on Saturday petitioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and chief electoral officer Archana Patnaik. He is seeking action against Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and TVK leader Aadhav Arjuna for allegedly violating the model code of conduct.

Article Title: Realty exec death: Court pulls up Gurgaon Police over ‘lapses’ in handling body
Article Text:
kada

ne jo kiya kiya





New Delhi: “The complainant not only lost her brother, but you took away her right to conduct the last rites,” a Delhi court observed Saturday, rebuking Gurgaon Police over the delayed uploading of ZIPNET details of the recovery and cremation of Delhi-based real estate executive Yuvraj Singh Manchanda’s body.Judicial magistrate First class Rahul Jain questioned sub-inspector Chandgi Ram of Badshahpur police station over the sequence of events leading to the cremation and sought an explanation for the delay in updating the portal.The court was hearing a plea by Manchanda’s sister, Harsimran, through senior advocate Amit Prasad and advocates Neharika Kushwah and Ayodhya Prasad, seeking preservation and production of records and digital material related to his death. The court reserved its order for Monday.Expressing dismay over the “shocking state of affairs”, Jain questioned the SI about why the nearest executive magistrate or sub-divisional magistrate was not informed on the second day after the recovery for inquest proceedings of the unidentified body.The judge also questioned the cremation of the body along with Manchanda’s belongings after the counsel submitted that a burnt watch andwere recovered from the site. “How can a body be cremated along with the belongings? Is this how you normally operate?” the court asked.Referring to the delay in updating details on ZIPNET, the portal used by police in the northern region to share information on missing persons and unidentified bodies, the court asked Gurgaon Police, “How were you to carry out the identification process after the body had been cremated?” The SI replied, “Doctor(The doctor who conducted the postmortem did everything).”The petitioner alleged that the police actions amounted to destruction of evidence and were intended to “save the culprits”. The counsel argued that the court had ancillary powers to issue directions regarding the handling of the body.The court flagged the absence of postmortem videography and discrepancies between two postmortem reports, one mentioning bullet injuries and the other attributing the cause of death to asphyxiation due to antemortem drowning. “How can you arrive at such different conclusions?” it asked.The judge also took note of the submission that the viscera had not been preserved during the postmortem.According to Delhi Police, Manchanda was last seen by his sisters on Sept 6 when he left for a meeting in Gurgaon. Delhi Police said he was murdered the same night by his former colleague Anya Vats and her partner, Sanyam Sachdeva. They have been remanded in 14-day judicial custody.
Article Summary: Delhi court rebukes Gurgaon Police over delayed uploading of ZIPNET details of the recovery and cremation of Delhi-based real estate executive Yuvraj Singh Manchanda’s body. Judge questions sub-inspector Chandgi Ram over the sequence of events leading to the cremation.

Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray seeks direct drought aid, CEC’s resignation during Marathwada tour
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray on Saturday demanded immediate, direct assistance for drought-hit farmers. He also stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll irregularities, saying his resignation alone would not be enough.“Those responsible for vote theft should face criminal action,” Thackeray said.Thackeray began a two-day tour of drought-hit Marathwada on Saturday. He visited farms and villages in Dharashiv and was scheduled to travel to Latur, Hingoli and other districts.“Govt has declared drought in 268 talukas. But the question is when and how will the assistance reach farmers,” he said.Thackeray claimed farmers were facing an exceptionally severe drought. He also alleged that assistance announced after last year’s excess rainfall and under loan-related measures had yet to reach many farmers.He backed Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray ’s demand for a special session of the state legislature to discuss the drought, drinking water shortages, problems in industrial areas and unemployment.Thackeray urged political parties, social organisations and NGOs to keep politics aside and reach farmers directly with assistance.He also alleged large-scale irregularities in electoral rolls. Thackeray claimed around 30 lakh of Mumbai’s 1.3 crore voters were fraudulent and that evidence regarding 17 lakh allegedly bogus voters had been submitted to the Election Commission ahead of the civic polls.“Gyanesh Kumar only says ‘yes sir’ to BJP,” Thackeray alleged. He said merely demanding the CEC’s resignation was not enough and sought criminal action against those responsible for the alleged irregularities.Thackeray said opposition parties would hold a major agitation in Mumbai on Oct 2 over alleged electoral irregularities and issues concerning the country’s youth.Sena (UBT) politicians Sushma Andhare, Ambadas Danve and party MLAs accompanied him on the tour.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray demanded immediate, direct assistance for drought-hit farmers. He also stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll irregularities. “Those responsible for vote theft should face criminal action,’ he said.

Article Title: ​Conman spins fake accident tale, dupes Beed official of Rs 30,000
Article Text:
TOI

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A fraudster allegedly took the sub-divisional officer of Majalgaon, in Beed, for a ride with an elaborate tale about the Mumbai collector’s son meeting with an accident. He claimed the injured man urgently needed an ambulance and money for hospitalisation.And the story came with just enough official-sounding backing to make it convincing. Majalgaon Rural police station in-charge Vijay Ramod said the fraudster first contacted the personal assistant of a former minister from Beed and sought “help”.“The PA then called the sub-divisional officer (SDO) and alerted him about the claimed accident in his jurisdiction. Soon, the fraudster contacted the SDOand asked for the money,” Ramod said.Two calls in quick succession did the trick. With little time to verify the story, the officer asked his brother to arrange for Rs 30,000.The money was paid immediately. Soon, however, doubts crept in.“After a few hours, the SDObecame suspicious. He contacted the Beed district collector to verify the alleged accident and learnt that no such incident had taken place,” Ramod said. By then, however, the conman had disappeared.Beed Rural police registered a case under BNS section 318(2) for cheating on Sept 21. Further investigation is underway..
Article Summary: A fraudster allegedly took the sub-divisional officer of Majalgaon, in Beed, for a ride with an elaborate tale. He claimed the injured man urgently needed an ambulance and money for hospitalisation. With little time to verify the story, the officer asked his brother to arrange for Rs 30,000.

Article Title: Uddhav should stop blaming ECI for his defeats: CM
Article Text:
CM Devendra Fadnavis

Kolhapur:





Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray should stop blaming Election Commission of India (ECI) ECI for his defeats and Mahayuti’s win in Maharashtra , chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday while speaking in Solapur.Asked about Thackeray’s demand for re-elections in Maharashtra and other states over ECI row, Fadnavis called it futile, citing the idiom: “The wound is on the forehead, but the bandage is tied to the knee”.“Why did he lose, why did people reject him? Instead of researching this, he only does one thing, that is, blaming the ECI. If Congress wins Telangana then ECI is doing a good job; if Congress wins Karnataka then ECI is good. But it is bad when Mahayuti wins in Maharashtra. This should stop,” Fadnavis said while speaking to the reporters in Solapur during a field visit to gauge the crop loss situation amid severe water scarcity.Addressing a news conference on Wednesday, Thackeray demanded sacking of chief election commissioner Dyanesh Kumar over alleged objections by the other two election commissioners.Lakhs of voters were added post-Lok Sabha election in Maharashtra suspiciously for the assembly election, which, according to him, led to Maha Vikas Aghadi’s defeat.The ECI, however, has denied the allegations. Thackeray said that Kumar’s conduct should also be probed.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray should stop blaming Election Commission of India (ECI) ECI for his defeats and Mahayuti’s win in Maharashtra, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday. “Why did he lose, why did people reject him? Instead of researching this, he only does one thing, that is, blaming the ECI. This should stop,” he said.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: PM classmate’s battle for land continues despite BJP MLA's exit, no possession yet
Article Text:
Asgar Ali Vora met the PM on Sept 8 and sought his intervention in the land disp­u­te





BHAYANDAR: Asgar Ali Vora, a schoolmate of Prime Minister Narendra Modi , continues to struggle to regain possession of his land after MLA Narendra Mehta’s company announced that it had relinquished the property. However, another developer is allegedly continuing to retain possession of the land.Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained against Mehta.Following the meeting, Mehta relinquished possession of the land, while the municipal corporation also cancelled the construction permission granted to him.However, the land has allegedly not been handed back to its original owner. Instead, developers Mukesh Parekh and Mervyn Fernandes are allegedly continuing to retain possession of the property. Following a complaint by Shiv Sena, Navghar police have registered a non-cognisable offence against Seven Eleven Constructions, Parekh and Fernandes.
Article Summary: Asgar Ali Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: 2 key accused arrested; 168 buyers on radar
Article Text:
Two key accused in TET paper leak case arrested

How the leak occured





BHIWANDI: Two key accused allegedly linked to 168 prospective buyers of the leaked Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) question paper have been arrested, nearly two months after police busted the racket, with the SIT now probing the wider network and possible transactions.The two — Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw, who was staying in Delhi — were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper, while Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers. The list was recovered from his Delhi residence.Shaw was arrested in Patna, Bihar, while Misal was arrested near Bhiwandi Naka on Sunday after police learnt he was planning to surrender before a court. Both were produced before the Bhiwandi court and remanded in police custody till Sept 23.The SIT has so far verified 18 of the 118 names on Shaw's list and found they were preparing to appear for the TET examination. Verification of the remaining 100 is underway.Police suspect Shaw was directly linked to Solapur-based coaching-class operator Prakash Pawar, who has already been arrested, and was also in contact with alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta.Investigators are questioning Misal to determine the price at which he allegedly planned to sell the paper and whether any sale took place. Earlier, accused Kapil Dahiya, who had allegedly travelled to Pune to deliver the paper to Misal, told investigators he could not hand it over.Police had busted the racket two days before the scheduled examination, forcing postponement of the TET.DCP Pawan Bansod confirmed the arrests. ACP Sachin Sangle, part of the SIT, told TOI, "Their interrogation will help us establish to whom they intended to sell the paper."Last week, the SIT filed a 3,470-page chargesheet before the Bhiwandi fast-track court against those arrested earlier in the case.With Misal and Shaw's arrests, police said the two remaining prominent accused identified during the investigation have been apprehended. Further arrests will depend on findings from their contacts and financial transactions.
Article Summary: Pune-based govt employee Prakash Misal and Bihar native Ashok Shaw were among the remaining prominent accused identified during the probe. Police said Misal was in touch with around 50 people who had shown interest in buying the paper. Shaw allegedly maintained a list of 118 prospective buyers.

Article Title: Cong neta seeks protection for 'gangrape' survivor, her kin
Article Text:
(Representative image)





THANE: A day after Padgha police registered an FIR against former Kalyan West MLA Narendra Pawar and dismissed policeman Shailesh Patil for allegedly gangraping a 22-year-old married woman at a farmhouse in Bapgaon, Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni on Friday sought police protection for the survivor and her family.Kulkarni, who accompanied the woman to the police station, claimed the survivor's life was in danger because of the accused's influence. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her.Meanwhile, Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence. Seperate police teams have also been formed to trace Pawar and Patil, who remain absconding. Pawar has denied the charge, calling them false. He has also resigned from all his BJP organisational posts. - Pradeep Gupta
Article Summary: Congress group leader in KDMC Kanchan Kulkarni sought police protection for the survivor and her family. She urged CM Eknath Shinde to intervene and ensure security for her. Padgha police conducted a spot panchnama at the farmhouse in Bapgaon to collect forensic evidence.

Article Title: Health camp at Madurai bench benefits 1,054
Article Text:
The camp was organised by the state health and family welfare department in association with the National Health Mission and the court. Blood samples were collected from 901 people on Sept 16, 21 and 22, while specialist consultations were held on Sept 24 and 25.

Madurai:





A total of 1,054 people benefited from a health camp conducted at the Madurai bench of Madras high court recently.The camp was organised by the state health and family welfare department in association with the National Health Mission and the court. Blood samples were collected from 901 people on Sept 16, 21 and 22, while specialist consultations were held on Sept 24 and 25.Nearly 20 specialist doctors and medical teams provided diagnostic services, clinical care and health evaluations to judges, registrars, govt pleaders, CISF personnel, state police officers, PWD officials and judicial staff of the Madurai bench.Justice A D Jagadish Chandira and Justice G R Swaminathan attended the event. National Health Mission director S Aneesh Sekhar and health department secretary Darez Ahmed were also present.
Article Summary: The camp was organised by the state health and family welfare department in association with the National Health Mission and the court. Blood samples were collected from 901 people on Sept 16, 21 and 22, while specialist consultations were held on Sept 24 and 25. Nearly 20 specialist doctors and medical teams provided diagnostic services, clinical care and health evaluations.

Article Title: HC reserves orders on plea by DMK man in Srirangam land fraud case
Article Text:
Madras high court on Friday reserved orders on the anticipatory bail plea of a DMK functionary who was booked in a Srirangam temple land fraud case.





Madurai: Madras high court on Friday reserved orders on the anticipatory bail plea of a DMK functionary who was booked in a Srirangam temple land fraud case.The court was hearing the anticipatory bail plea of a DMK functionary, N Ramkumar, who was booked by the Trichy city crime branch police.The case of the prosecution is that the petitioner is alleged to have illegally grabbed a 7,515 sq ft land parcel belonging to Srirangam temple in Vellithirumutttam village in Srirangam taluk, Trichy district. Based on the complaint lodged by the temple’s joint commissioner/executive officer, police registered a case against six people, including the petitioner and the sub-registrar.In his petition, the petitioner stated that he is a bona fide purchaser of the property. The claim of the executive officer of the temple that the property belongs to the temple is factually incorrect.The counsel for the executive officer of the temple objected to the grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner. The state also objected to the grant of anticipatory bail, stating that custodial interrogation is warranted in this case.After elaborately hearing the arguments, Justice K Murali Shankar reserved orders.
Article Summary: DMK functionary, N Ramkumar, was booked by the Trichy city crime branch police. He is alleged to have illegally grabbed a 7,515 sq ft land parcel belonging to Srirangam temple in Vellithirumutttam village.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: Man arrested for bike theft in Kochi
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Puthencruz Police arrested a 46-year-old man in connection with a motorcycle theft case on Saturday. Ajith Kumar of Perumpuzha, Kollam, is the arrested person.The accused allegedly stole a motorcycle belonging to the complainant, who was staying in a rented house in the Kolenchery area, on March 31. The vehicle had been parked in the courtyard of the house.The accused, who had been absconding and hiding in the Uduma area of Kasaragod, was traced through scientific investigation methods, said the police.The police said that other cases are also pending against him at the Kundara and Kollam West police stations.In Nov 2025, he was externed from Kollam district for eight months under Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act.Deputy superintendent of police N Babukuttan, inspector M P Eby, sub-inspectors Jithin Kumar, G Sasidharan, Manoj Kumar and Biju John, and senior civil police officer K R Akhil were part of the investigation team.
Article Summary: Ajith Kumar of Perumpuzha, Kollam, is the arrested person. The accused allegedly stole a motorcycle belonging to the complainant, who was staying in a rented house in the Kolenchery area. The vehicle had been parked in the courtyard of the house.
